before:
import afield.lang.solidsl.*
import afield.geometry.solid.manifold.ManifoldLibrary
import afield.geometry.mesh.MeshView
import afield.geometry.mesh.isWatertight

// ---- a part that is half CSG and half field -------------------------------------------
// A plate you could machine, unioned with a blob you could not: the fillet where the ball
// meets the post lies on NEITHER of them, so no sequence of unions, intersections and
// differences can produce it. The exact lowering says so instead of guessing.
val fillet = 0.28

val machinable = cuboid(3.2, 3.2, 0.5) - unionOf(
    listOf(-1.1 to -1.1, 1.1 to -1.1, -1.1 to 1.1, 1.1 to 1.1).map { (x, y) ->
        cylinder(2.0, 0.22, segments = 128).at(x, y, 0.0)
    },
)
val organic = smoothUnion(
    sphere(0.62, segments = 128).at(0.0, 0.0, 0.95),
    cylinder(1.6, 0.28, segments = 128).at(0.0, 0.0, 0.45),
    k = fillet,
)
val part = machinable + organic
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

run {

println("---- what this expression refuses, and why ----")
part.allRefusals().forEach {
    println("  ${it.node}")
    println("    ${it.why}")
    println("    closable: ${it.closable}${if (it.missing.isNotBlank()) " — needs ${it.missing}" else ""}")
}
if (part.allRefusals().isEmpty()) println("  (nothing — every node has an exact CSG form)")
println()

// The catalogue, and why the last two refusals are a different kind from the first two.
println("The catalogue, in full — try each of these:")
listOf<Pair<String, SolidExpr>>(
    "smoothUnion(a, b, k)" to smoothUnion(sphere(1.0), cuboid(1.0, 1.0, 1.0), k = 0.2),
    "gyroid()" to gyroid(),
    "sphere(1).rounded(0.1)" to sphere(1.0).rounded(0.1),
    "sphere(1).shelled(0.05)" to sphere(1.0).shelled(0.05),
).forEach { (label, e) ->
    println("  %-24s %s".format(label, e.exactRefusal()!!.why.take(96) + "…"))
}
println()
println("The last two are the interesting ones. They are NOT 'we did not get to it': an")
println("exact-looking answer is available — Minkowski sum with a sphere — and it is the")
println("WRONG answer, systematically, by up to that sphere's sagitta, in a direction that")
println("does not shrink as the march refines. Filing that beside a smooth blend would")
println("flatten a real distinction, so the reason says which kind it is.")
println()

if (!ManifoldLibrary.isAvailable) {
    println(ManifoldLibrary.describe())
    return@run
}

// ---- the hybrid: the level set applied at the SMALLEST subtree that needs it -----------
// A naive fallback asks "does the whole tree lower exactly?" and marches everything if the
// answer is no — so one smooth blend anywhere costs a hundred-thousand-triangle
// approximation of a plate that was perfectly exact. This walks down instead.
val q = SolidQuality(segments = 128, edgeLengthFraction = 1.0 / 90.0)
val build = part.buildSolid(q)
println("---- the hybrid build ----")
println(build.report())
println()

// What the naive version would have cost: one level set over the whole part, same edge length.
val raw = part.bounds()!!
val edge = maxOf(raw.size.x, raw.size.y, raw.size.z) / 90.0
val naive = afield.geometry.solid.manifold.Solid.levelSet(raw.expandedBy(2.0 * edge), edge, parallel = true) { x, y, z ->
    part.toLevelSetField().at(x, y, z)
}
println("hybrid  ${build.solid.triangleCount} triangles")
println("naive   ${naive.triangleCount} triangles for the same shape at the same edge length")
println("        — ${"%.2f".format(naive.triangleCount.toDouble() / build.solid.triangleCount)}x, and " +
    "the plate's six faces stay six faces")
println()

val mesh = build.solid.toTriMesh()
println("Field's own topology, sharing nothing with Manifold: watertight ${mesh.isWatertight()}")
println("status ${build.solid.status} — guaranteed closed however the field behaved")

showMesh(
    build.solid.toTriMesh(normals = true),
    channel = "hybrid",
    title = "exact where it can be, marched where it cannot",
    caption = "${build.solid.triangleCount} triangles · the plate and its four bores are exact CSG; " +
        "only the blended post was marched · the whole thing is still one guaranteed-closed solid",
    view = MeshView(yawDegrees = 36.0, pitchDegrees = 22.0, width = 720, height = 470),
)
naive.close()
build.close()

}

before:
import afield.lang.solidsl.*
import afield.geometry.mesh.MeshView

// ---- the problem ---------------------------------------------------------------------
// Somebody hands you a bag of points with a signed distance at each. What shape is it?
val truth = doubleArrayOf(0.45, 1.90, 0.16)     // the answer, used ONLY to make the target
val seed = doubleArrayOf(0.26, 1.05, 0.34)      // where the search starts: wrong by 42%, 45%, 112%
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

val template = smoothUnion(sphere(0.45), cylinder(1.90, 0.16).at(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), k = 0.18)
    .parameterize {
        param("sphereRadius", "SmoothUnion/a/Sphere.radius")
        param("barHeight", "SmoothUnion/b/Translate/Cylinder.height")
        param("barRadius") { it.node == "Cylinder" && it.field.startsWith("radius") }
    }.orThrow()

val target = template.withValues(truth).sampleField(count = 2400, seed = 91)
println("target: $target")
println()

// One tape per evaluation carries all 2400 residuals and all 3 parameters, and one backward
// sweep reads every derivative off it. The alternative — central-differencing the loss —
// costs 2n extra full sweeps per step and needs an fdStep tuned per problem.
val fit = template.fitParameters(target, seed)
println(fit.report())
println()
println("The counterfactual is in the same object, measured in the same run: `initialLoss`")
println("is the seed's loss, not a number somebody wrote down last week.")
println()
println("truth was  ${truth.joinToString(", ")}")
println("recovered  ${fit.values.joinToString(", ") { "%.9f".format(it) }}")
println("error      ${truth.indices.joinToString(", ") { "%.2e".format(kotlin.math.abs(fit.values[it] - truth[it])) }}")
println()

// The fitted answer is an ordinary SolidExpr again — not a bag of numbers — so it goes
// straight back to every other thing this package can do.
println("fitted     ${fit.fitted}")
println("GLSL       ${fit.fitted.toGlsl().statementCount} statements")
println("bounds     ${fit.fitted.bounds()}")
println()

// Log scale, because the descent covers twenty orders of magnitude and a linear axis
// would be a vertical line at iteration 0 followed by a flat one.
showSignals("ln(loss)" to fit.run.losses.map { kotlin.math.ln(it + 1e-30) })

val view = MeshView(yawDegrees = 32.0, pitchDegrees = 22.0, width = 660, height = 430)
showMesh(
    template.withValues(seed).march(resolution = 110),
    channel = "seed",
    title = "the seed - where the search started",
    caption = "%.2f, %.2f, %.2f · loss %.4e".format(seed[0], seed[1], seed[2], fit.initialLoss),
    view = view,
)
showMesh(
    fit.fitted.march(resolution = 110),
    channel = "fitted",
    title = "the fit - what the gradient found",
    caption = "%.6f, %.6f, %.6f · loss %.4e · %.3g times better".format(
        fit.values[0], fit.values[1], fit.values[2], fit.loss, fit.improvementFactor,
    ),
    view = view,
)
showMesh(
    template.withValues(truth).march(resolution = 110),
    channel = "target",
    title = "the target - the shape the samples came from",
    caption = "%.2f, %.2f, %.2f · the fitted render above is pixel-identical to this one".format(
        truth[0], truth[1], truth[2],
    ),
    view = view,
)
